compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` in `src/rebar/llm/config.py` maps the `gemini` prefix to the provider name
`google_genai`, but no runtime registry knows that name, so any bare `gemini-*` model id resolves to
a provider that cannot be constructed and dies at call time.

Reproduced on this base (worktree at `origin/main`, `d72c477`):

    infer_provider('gemini-2.5-pro')                 -> 'google_genai'
    'google_genai' in _pydantic_ai_known_providers() -> False
    'google_genai' in KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES           -> False
    ProviderSession(LLMConfig())._builders           -> ['anthropic', 'bedrock']
    ProviderSession.is_resolvable('google_genai')    -> False
    ProviderSession.provider_factory('google_genai') -> LLMConfigError:
        unknown provider 'google_genai'; registered providers: ['anthropic', 'bedrock']

pydantic-ai 1.107.1 recognises `google`, `google-cloud`, `google-gla`, `google-vertex`, `vertexai`
and `gateway/google-cloud`. It does NOT recognise `google_genai`.

### Which path actually breaks

There are two composition sites, and only one of them is broken — this matters for where the test
goes:

- `anthropic_model._pai_model()` (used by `runner.run()` for a BARE `cfg.model`) passes the inferred
  name through a second, private table, `_PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX`, which happens to translate
  `google_genai -> google-gla`. That path accidentally survives.
- `model_classes._resolve_target()` — the model-class / ladder path (`trivial = { model =
  "gemini-2.5-pro" }`, fallback chains, `resolve_model_string`) — uses `infer_provider`'s result
  VERBATIM and composes `google_genai:gemini-2.5-pro`. `_pai_model` then returns that string
  unchanged because it is already qualified, and provider construction raises. This is the
  end-to-end failure and is what the RED test must exercise.

The failure is at CALL time, not config time: an operator who configures a `gemini-*` model gets a
plausible-looking config that fails only when a gate actually runs.

## Design decision

**Map `gemini` to `google`.** `google` is pydantic-ai's current canonical provider name for the
Gemini Developer API; `google:gemini-*` ids appear directly in `known_model_names()`, and `google`
is already a member of both `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` and `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()`, so
`ProviderSession.is_resolvable('google')` is True and the model is left on the existing deferred
lazy-string path (rebar registers no builder for it, exactly as for `openai` without a `base_url`).
Building it still requires the optional `google-genai` package, and pydantic-ai's own ImportError
already names the extra to install — that is the same contract every other delegate provider has,
not a new failure mode.

Rejected alternatives:

- `google-gla` / `google-vertex` / `vertexai` — resolvable, but pydantic-ai 1.107.1 emits a
  deprecation warning for these prefixes and removes them in v2.0, so choosing one would
  re-introduce a scheduled break.
- Dropping the `gemini` prefix entirely so a bare `gemini-*` id fails at config time — this yields a
  WORSE outcome for an operator who has the Google extra installed: a model that pydantic-ai can
  serve today would stop being usable via a bare id.
- Adding `google_genai` to `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` (what 7b22's plan proposes for a back-compat test)
  — rejected: it makes a name that neither pydantic-ai nor rebar can build a first-class member, and
  `ProviderSession` would still refuse it. 7b22 must not lock that choice in.

`anthropic_model._PAI_PROVIDER_PREFIX` is deliberately NOT touched. Its `google_genai` key becomes
unreachable from inference but is still a valid explicit-`model_provider` back-compat shim, and
`capabilities.py` documents its `google-gla` output as load-bearing. Changing it is a separate
concern from making the inference table agree with the registries.

## Changes

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES`: `("gemini", "google_genai")` becomes
  `("gemini", "google")`; update the two comments that restate the old mapping (the
  `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` preamble and the `LLMConfig.model_provider` comment).
- `tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py` — replace `test_the_inference_path_is_not_validated`
  (which pins the defect as deliberately out of scope) with the fixed expectation; add the
  whole-table invariant and the regression pins.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_framework.py` — `test_infer_provider` pins
  `infer_provider("gemini-2.5-pro") == "google_genai"`; update to the resolvable name.

## Test plan

1. RED first, on the end-to-end mechanism: assert
   `model_classes._resolve_target("gemini-2.5-pro", None)` composes a provider string that
   `ProviderSession(LLMConfig()).is_resolvable(...)` accepts. On unfixed code this fails with
   `google_genai`.
2. AC2 invariant, parameterized over the WHOLE `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` table (not just the gemini
   entry): every mapped provider name is in `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` or in
   `ProviderSession._builders`, so a future added prefix cannot reintroduce the class of defect.
3. AC3 regression pins: `claude-* -> anthropic`, `gpt-*/chatgpt-* -> openai`, an already-qualified
   `google-gla:gemini-2.5-flash` still passes through unchanged, an unknown id still infers `None`.
4. Mutation-check in both directions: revert the one-line production change and confirm the new
   tests go RED; restore and confirm GREEN.
5. Gates by exit code: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the default `pytest` selection.

## Risk and rollback

One-line data change in a lookup table plus test updates; no control flow changes. Blast radius is
limited to model ids that begin with `gemini`, which today cannot work at all. Rollback is reverting
the single commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A bare `gemini-*` model id resolves, through both `infer_provider` and
  `model_classes._resolve_target`, to a provider name that `ProviderSession.is_resolvable` accepts.
- AC2: No value in `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` maps to a provider name absent from both
  `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()` and `ProviderSession._builders`. A test pins this for the WHOLE
  table, not just the gemini entry, so the next added prefix cannot reintroduce the class of defect.
- AC3: Inference for `claude-*`, `gpt-*`/`chatgpt-*`, already-qualified ids, and unknown ids is
  unchanged, pinned by test.
- AC4: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default pytest selection is green.
